title: Extent of Election Campaigning and Similar Activities Following Issuance of Writ of Election
what_it_is: Extent of Election Campaigning and Similar Activities Following Issuance of Writ of Election

sections.label: Election campaigning outside campaign period
sections.summary: Election laws regulate campaigning only during the campaign period, so outside it parties and candidates may conduct activities if they comply with other laws.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Our election laws primarily regulate campaigning during the campaign period, which commences from the closure of the place of nomination on Nomination Day and ends at the start of the eve of Polling Day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Outside of the campaign period, the election laws do not prohibit political parties and aspiring candidates from conducting activities, such as house-to-house visits; visiting markets and coffee shops to interact with residents; or to explicitly canvass for votes while wearing their party uniforms and badges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This is assuming that these activities comply with the other laws of the land.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For example, election advertising must comply with the prevailing publishing requirements and non-Singapore Citizens must not publish or display election advertising.

sections.label: Interactions and electoral advertising rules
sections.summary: Anyone may interact with residents at any time if laws are followed, and electoral advertising rules apply during the election period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Anyone can interact with any residents at any time of the year, so long as it complies with the laws of the land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, in answer to the first supplementary question that Mr Gerald Giam asked, what is the difference between the period from the Writ of Election to the nomination, the details can be found in the guidebook that we have published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, during the election period, there are rules that governs the electoral advertising – what can be done and what cannot be done, as part of electoral advertising.
